acceptanceCriteria: A forward migration adds the ten identifiers in the Scope table to the allowed values of `resumes.template`. The five existing values stay allowed and no stored row changes. The checked-in generated types list the fifteen values.
Until its own story lands, each of the other nine identifiers is offered nowhere: not in the template picker, not accepted by the job-application and AI routes, not accepted by the Word route.

`swissVocational` appears in the template picker after the five existing templates, with its live thumbnail and its fr, en, de and it name and description. A CV can be created with it from the new-CV page and from a job application.

The Editor live preview, the Preview page, the PDF and the Word export of a `swissVocational` CV match `t1-cfc.png`: Page and accent: one column, with a thin red accent at the left edge. Header: name, CV title and contact details on the left, photo top right. The contact details show labelled address, phone, e-mail and LinkedIn. Section order: summary, experience, education, continuing education (certifications), then skills and languages side by side. Dated sections: the dates sit in a left column.

FR-2: Items with `visible: false` and sections hidden through the existing layout settings are absent from the Editor live preview, the Preview page, the PDF and the Word export. An empty section, including one whose items are all hidden, is not drawn: no heading without content.

userStories.title: The "Commerce & administration" template is available
userStories.description: As an office or administration professional, I want a sober template built for commercial and administrative roles, so that my organisational and office skills stand out.
acceptanceCriteria: `swissCommerce` appears in the template picker after `swissVocational`, with its localized name and description. A CV can be created with it.

The Editor live preview, the Preview page, the PDF and the Word export match `t2-commerce.png`: Header: a full-width navy band holding a round photo, the name, the CV title and the contact details. Body: one column, with the dates of dated sections in a left column. Skills: in two columns. Languages: as labelled pills.
The template satisfies FR-1 to FR-11.

FR-1: A template renders only data already stored for the resume (the fields listed in Context). It writes nothing back and adds no new stored state; its only output is the rendered CV. Sample text is never hard-coded into a template.

FR-2: Items with `visible: false` and sections hidden through the existing layout settings are absent from the Editor live preview, the Preview page, the PDF and the Word export. An empty section, including one whose items are all hidden, is not drawn: no heading without content.

FR-3: The template's section order is the order its story states. The template is registered in `TEMPLATE_LAYOUT_CONTROLS` and `TEMPLATE_EDITOR_SECTIONS` with only controls whose effect it actually draws. A control it does not draw is not offered.

FR-4 (amended): A Swiss template uses its own typeface (the face its story names, otherwise the platform default) at font scale 1.0 in all four outputs. It ignores the stored font family and font scale, and leaves them stored unchanged, so switching back to an existing template restores them. The font carousel and font-size slider are not offered for it (FR-3).

FR-5 (amended): When the CV has a photo and the photo tick of FR-14 is on, every template except `swissAcademic` draws it at the place and in the shape its mockup shows, in all four outputs. No photo, or photo unticked: no photo frame in any of the four outputs, the Editor live preview included. Upload: from the Contact tab photo row (FR-14), reusing the existing photo upload handler and storage. No upload box is drawn inside the CV.

FR-6: Section headings use the existing `resumes.template` labels. Three new labels are added in fr, en, de and it, and are used only by the new templates: `projects` ("Projets"); `publications` ("Publications et projets"); `distinctions` ("Distinctions"). A heading whose wording in a mockup differs from an existing label uses the existing label. For example, "Profil" in a mockup reads as the summary label.

FR-7: Language levels use the existing level values, shown with the existing localized level names. Where `swissFirstJob` draws dots, the filled count is: Native 5, Fluent 4, Professional 3, Intermediate 2, Basic 1.
FR-8: The name and description of each template live in `resumes.templates` of all four `common.json` files. `templateLabels` finds them, and the locale-parity and template-name tests cover them.

FR-9: Rich text (summary, descriptions, `skillsHtml`) is rendered through the same sanitizing and formatting helpers that the existing templates use for each output. The Preview stays server-renderable (no SSR-unsafe call in the template's render path).

FR-10: The Word export of a template is produced by its own generator. The export: contains every visible section and item of the Preview, in the same order; draws the photo per FR-5; follows the template's layout (columns, header band, colours) to the degree Word supports it. Any difference from the Preview is recorded as a validation finding, not assumed acceptable.

FR-11: In its own story, a template's identifier is added to every list that offers or accepts the existing templates: `TEMPLATE_OPTIONS`; `RESUME_TEMPLATES` in the job-application route; `validTemplates` in the AI route; `SUPPORTED_TEMPLATES` in the Word route.
FR-12 (amendment 1): The Editor shows the font carousel and font-size slider only for templates whose rendering applies them: the five existing templates, not the Swiss ones.

FR-13 (amendment 1): The Preview page has no "Show Controls" switch and no per-element size handles, for any template. The Preview renders the stored layout values read-only. The now-unused `showControls` locale key is removed from all four locales together.

FR-14 (amendment 1): Contact visibility is stored in the existing `layout_settings` value as `hiddenContactFields`. The property is a list drawn only from `title`, `email`, `phone`, `location`, `linkedin`, `github`, `website` and `photo`. Missing or empty: everything is shown, so existing CVs render exactly as before. Validation: unknown entries are dropped by the existing validation in `src/lib/layout-settings.ts`, and the value stays within the existing 4096-byte bound. Readers: the Editor live preview, the Preview page, the PDF and every Word generator, all reading this same value. No second copy is kept. Labels: tick-box labels are localized in fr, en, de and it.

FR-15 (amendment 2): In `swissVocational`, a skill category's label and its skills are two stacked blocks: the label on its own line, the skills below it at the full column width. The Editor live preview, the Preview page, the PDF and the `swissVocational` Word generator draw the same structure. The stored skill data, the other Swiss templates' skills layouts (defined by their own stories) and the five existing templates are unchanged.

Regression constraint: With every contact tick on (the default), the five existing templates render, export to PDF and export to Word exactly as before: their visual baselines in `e2e/visual` do not change, except where a baseline captures the Preview page's "Show Controls" switch or its handles (FR-13). Each such change is listed and shown in that story's evidence; `pnpm test:parity` keeps its verdicts for them (MATCH 211, KNOWN 3, NEW 0 at origin/main f0a2e75).
Regression constraint: Existing resumes keep their stored template. A CV created before the migration opens, edits, previews and exports unchanged.
Regression constraint: The template picker keeps its radio-group keyboard behaviour across all fifteen options, and its existing order for the first five.

Regression constraint: The photo upload handler, the background removal and the photo's storage key are unchanged. `modern` keeps its existing upload zone and also gains the Contact-tab photo row (FR-14).
Regression constraint: The cover letter templates are unchanged.

Regression constraint: Amendment 2 changes only the skills section of `swissVocational`. Its `e2e/visual` baseline is updated in US-012 for that section alone, and the evidence shows the old and new baseline side by side. Every other baseline, and every parity verdict, stays unchanged.

Verification: Browser evidence, for each template: What is captured: the Editor live preview, the Preview page, and the picker card with its thumbnail. Data: a sample CV filled in every field the template draws, plus a variant with hidden items and empty sections, plus a variant with and without a photo. Locales: at least fr and one other locale. Comparison: side by side with the template's mockup.

Verification: Export evidence, for each template: Artifacts: a generated PDF and a generated `.docx`, both inspected. Content: every visible section and item present, in order, and hidden content absent. Photo: present or absent per FR-5. Word layout: checked against the Preview at the strength the available renderer allows; a limit is reported as a finding.
Verification: Visual: a new `e2e/visual` baseline for each new template, created in its story; the existing baselines unchanged.
Verification: Unit: tests for each template's Word generator, the language-dot mapping (FR-7), the registry entries (FR-3, FR-8) and the template lists of the job and AI routes.

FAIL condition: A hidden item or section appears in any of the four outputs, or a heading appears with no content under it.
FAIL condition: The Word export omits, reorders or rewrites visible content, or the PDF differs from the Preview.

FAIL condition: A template name, description or heading is missing or untranslated in one of fr, en, de or it.
FAIL condition: A template's Preview returns a non-200 response on the server render.

Out of scope: Any new resume field, column, JSON property or stored setting, including nationality, permit, date of birth, skill level or a CEFR language level. Sole exception (amendment 1): the contact-visibility list of FR-14, stored inside the existing `layout_settings` value.

Out of scope: Any change to the five existing templates, their Word generators, their layout controls or their visual and parity baselines. Exceptions (amendment 1): the contact-visibility ticks of FR-14 apply to them, and the Preview page loses its "Show Controls" switch (FR-13), for every template.

Out of scope: Any change to the Editor's form fields, sections or save behavior, other than the Contact-tab ticks and photo row of FR-12 and FR-14; the photo storage, its upload handler or its background removal; the PDF rendering pipeline; or the cover letter.

Out of scope: A version bump.
